text: If the perimeter of a circle is equal to that of a square, then the ratio of their areas is

explain.why: Let the circle have radius r. Its perimeter is 2πr, so the square has side πr/2. The areas are πr² for the circle and π²r²/4 for the square. The ratio is 4 : π, which with π = 22/7 is 28 : 22 = 14 : 11.

options.A: That is π itself, 22 : 7.
options.C: That is 1/π, 7 : 22.
options.D: That is the ratio the other way round, square to circle.

text: The area of a circle A is the sum of areas of two small circles of diameter 10cm and 24 cm, the diameter of the circle A is?

explain.why: The area of the big circle is π(5² + 12²) = 169π, so its radius is 13 and its diameter is 26. The small circles have radii 5 and 12.

options.A: That is 24 − 10, the difference of the two diameters.
options.C: That is 5 + 12, the sum of the two radii.
options.D: That is the sum of the two diameters, 10 + 24.

text: If a couple of dice are thrown together what will be the probability of getting the same number on both dice?

explain.why: Of the 36 outcomes of two dice, 6 have the same number on both: (1,1) to (6,6). The probability is 6/36 = 1/6.

options.B: That is the chance of one particular pair, such as (3, 3).
options.C: That is 3/36.
options.D: That is 12/36.

text: The sum of the first 10 odd natural numbers is ____.

explain.why: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n². For 10 numbers it is 100: 1 + 3 + 5 + ... + 19.

options.A: That is 10 × 20.
options.B: That is 10 × 21.
options.D: That is 20².

text: What is the smallest number divisible by both 18 and 57?

explain.why: 18 = 2 × 3² and 57 = 3 × 19. The smallest common multiple has 2, 3² and 19: 2 × 9 × 19 = 342.

options.A: 400 is not divisible by 18.
options.B: 350 is not divisible by 18.
options.C: 260 is not divisible by 18.

text: Total number of factors any prime number has?

explain.why: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.

options.A: Would be right for the square of a prime, such as 9, which has the factors 1, 3 and 9.
options.C: Every number has at least the factor 1, so 0 is not possible.
options.D: That would be true only for the number 1.

text: The HFC of 12 and 18 is?

explain.why: HCF stands for the highest common factor. 12 = 2² × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3², so the HCF is 2 × 3 = 6.

options.A: 2 is a common factor, but not the highest.
options.B: 3 is a common factor, but not the highest.
options.C: 4 does not divide 18.

text: If two dice are thrown together what is the probability of getting an even number on both dice?

explain.why: Each die is even with probability 3/6 = 1/2. For both dice, 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.

options.A: That is 6/36, the chance of the same number on both.
options.B: That is the chance of one particular pair.
options.D: That is the chance of an even number on one die.

text: If a number between 1 and 30 is chosen at random what is the probability of getting a prime number?

explain.why: The primes from 1 to 30 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23 and 29: 10 of the 30 numbers. The probability is 10/30 = 1/3.

options.A: That is 20/30, the chance of a number that is not prime.
options.C: That is 5/30.
options.D: The probability is 10/30, which is 1/3, not 11/13.

text: What is the next number in the sequence 4, 8, 16, _?

explain.why: Each term is twice the one before: 4, 8, 16, so the next is 32.

options.A: That adds 4 each time, which does not fit 4 → 8 → 16.
options.B: That adds 8 to 16, which does not fit the pattern.
options.C: Would be right if the differences were 4, 8, 12, which is not the pattern.

text: What will be the sum of the sequence up to 5th term 9, 36, 144, 576, ...?

explain.why: Each term is 4 times the one before, so the 5th term is 576 × 4 = 2304. The sum is 9 + 36 + 144 + 576 + 2304 = 3069.

text: The diameter of the circle is 10cm. What will be the perimeter of the shape(Use pi = 3.14)?

explain.why: The perimeter of a circle with diameter 10 cm is π × 10 = 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm.

options.B: That is the circumference plus one diameter, 31.4 + 10.
options.C: That is the circumference plus two diameters, 31.4 + 20.
options.D: That is the circumference plus three diameters, 31.4 + 30.

text: Choose the odd one out of the following 2, 3, 5, and 6.

explain.why: 2, 3 and 5 are prime numbers. 6 is not prime, so 6 is the odd one out.

options.A: 2 is prime.
options.B: 3 is prime.
options.C: 5 is prime.

text:
Which of the following is an Armstrong number?
(Armstrong number is a number that is equal to the sum of cubes of its digits.)

explain.why: 407 is an Armstrong number: 4³ + 0³ + 7³ = 64 + 0 + 343 = 407.

text: The sum of the first ten natural numbers is?

explain.why: The sum of the first n natural numbers is n(n + 1)/2. For n = 10 it is 10 × 11 / 2 = 55.

options.A: That is the sum of 1 to 9.
options.B: That is 9 × 6, not 10 × 11 / 2.
options.D: That is 10 × 6, not 10 × 11 / 2.

text: A couple of dice is rolled together. What is the probability of getting the same number on both dice?

explain.why: Of the 36 outcomes of two dice, 6 have the same number on both. The probability is 6/36 = 1/6.

options.B: That is the chance of one particular pair.
options.C: That is 12/36.
options.D: That would mean the dice always match.

text: What is the Least Common Multiple of 4 & 8?

explain.why: The least common multiple of 4 and 8 is 8, since 8 is already a multiple of 4.

options.A: 2 divides both, but it is not a multiple of 8.
options.C: 12 is not a multiple of 8.
options.D: 16 is a common multiple, but not the least.

text:
The area of circle A is equal to the sum of the area of two small circles with diameters of 6cm and 8cm. Then the diameter of
circle A will be?

explain.why: The area of circle A is π(3² + 4²) = 25π, so its radius is 5 and its diameter is 10.

options.A: That is the radius.
options.C: A diameter of 15 would need an area of 56.25π, not 25π.
options.D: A diameter of 20 would need an area of 100π, not 25π.

text: What are the prime factors of the number 124

explain.why: 124 = 2 × 62 = 2 × 2 × 31. The prime factors are 2 and 31, as 62 is not prime.

options.A: 62 is not prime; it is 2 × 31.
options.C: 124 is not prime, and 1 is not a prime.
options.D: 2 and 31 are the prime factors.

text: What is the Lowest Common multiple of 5,15

explain.why: 15 is a multiple of 5, so the lowest common multiple of 5 and 15 is 15.

options.A: 5 is not a multiple of 15.
options.B: 10 is not a multiple of 15.
options.D: 20 is not a multiple of 15.

text: A car traveled 281 km in 4 hours 41 minutes. What was the average speed of the car in km per minute?

explain.why: 4 hours 41 minutes is 4 × 60 + 41 = 281 minutes. The car goes 281 km in 281 minutes, which is 1 km per minute.

options.B: 281 km in 281 minutes is 1 km per minute, not 2.
options.C: 281 km in 281 minutes is 1 km per minute, not 3.
options.D: 281 km in 281 minutes is 1 km per minute, not 4.

text: The length of a rectangle is four times its width. If the area is 100m2 what is the width of the rectangle?

explain.why: If the width is w, the length is 4w and the area is 4w² = 100. So w² = 25 and the width is 5 m.

options.A: 10 is the square root of 100, which ignores the factor 4.
options.C: A width of 4 gives an area of 4 × 16 = 64.
options.D: A width of 6 gives an area of 6 × 24 = 144.

text: The length of a rectangle is increased to 2 times its original size and its width is increased to 3 times its original size. If the area of the new rectangle is equal to 1800 square meters, what is the area of the original rectangle?

explain.why: The new length is 2 times and the new width is 3 times, so the new area is 2 × 3 = 6 times the old one. The original area is 1800 / 6 = 300 square metres.

options.A: That is 1800 × 2 / 3.
options.B: The area changes when the sides change.
options.D: Would be right if the area grew 9 times, not 6 (1800 / 9).

text: Water is being pumped out , at a constant rate, from an underground storage tank that has a height 5 Meters. Which of the graphs below best represent the changes in the height of water in the tank as a function of the time (X axis - Time, Y axis - Height)?

explain.why: The water is pumped out at a constant rate, so the height falls evenly from 5 m to 0, a straight line going down. That is graph A.

options.B: That is a vertical line: the height would drop at once.
options.C: That is a flat line: the height would not change.
options.D: That is a line going up: the height would rise.

text: Rama drove at a constant speed for 2 hours. He then stopped for an hour to do some shopping and have a rest and then drove back home driving at a constant speed. Which graph best represents the changes in the distance from home as Rama was driving (X axis - Time, Y axis - Distance)?

explain.why: Rama drives away at a steady speed for 2 hours (distance goes up), stops for an hour (distance stays flat) and drives home (distance goes down to 0). That is graph B.

options.A: That starts at a distance and falls first.
options.C: That keeps going up after the stop; he never returns home.
options.D: That is a flat line: he does not move.

text: In a certain college, 40% of a class are taking Physics, 30% are taking calculus and 10% are taking both. If 40 students are enrolled in the class, how many students are taking neither Physics nor calculus?

explain.why: Of 40 students, 16 take Physics (40%), 12 take calculus (30%) and 4 take both (10%). Taking either is 16 + 12 − 4 = 24, so 40 − 24 = 16 take neither.

options.A: That is the number taking calculus.
options.B: That is the number taking both.
options.C: That is 20% of 40; the students taking neither are 40% of the class, 16.

text: The circumference of a circle inscribed inside a square with a side of 20 meters.

explain.why: A circle inside a square of side 20 m touches all four sides, so its diameter is 20 m. The circumference is π × 20 = 20π.

options.A: That is the circumference for a diameter of 10.
options.B: Would be right for a circle with a diameter of 10√2.
options.D: That uses the diagonal of the square, 20√2, as the diameter.

text: Two different schools (A and B) have the same number of pupils. The ratio of the boys in school A and the boys in school B is 2:1 and the ratio of the girls in school A and the girls in school B is 4:5. Find the ratio of the boys in school A to the girls in school A.

explain.why: Let the boys in A be 2x and in B be x, and the girls in A be 4y and in B be 5y. The schools have equal pupils, so 2x + 4y = x + 5y, so x = y. Boys A : girls A = 2x : 4y = 2x : 4x = 1 : 2.

options.A: With x = y the ratio of boys to girls in A is 2x : 4x, which is 1 : 2.
options.B: With x = y the ratio of boys to girls in A is 2x : 4x, which is 1 : 2.
options.C: With x = y the ratio of boys to girls in A is 2x : 4x, which is 1 : 2.

text: What is the circumference of a circle inscribed inside a rectangle with a length of 8 meters and breadth of 4 meters ?

explain.why: A circle inside an 8 m × 4 m rectangle is limited by the shorter side, so its diameter is 4 m. The circumference is π × 4 = 12.57 m.

options.B: That is the circumference for a diameter of 8.
options.C: That is the circumference for a diameter of 2.
options.D: That is the circumference for a diameter of 16, not 4.

text: What is the sum of the first 27 odd numbers?

explain.why: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n². For 27 numbers it is 27² = 729.

options.A: The sum of the first 27 odd numbers is 27² = 729, not this.
options.C: That is only the number of terms.
options.D: The sum of the first 27 odd numbers is 27² = 729, not this.

text: What is the Least Common Multiple of 12 and 8?

explain.why: 12 = 2² × 3 and 8 = 2³. The least common multiple is 2³ × 3 = 24.

options.A: 2 divides both, but it is not a multiple of them.
options.B: 12 is not a multiple of 8.
options.C: 8 is not a multiple of 12.

text: If the length of the square is thrice its original length, its perimeter will be 120 meters. What is the original length of the square?

explain.why: A square of side 3L has perimeter 4 × 3L = 12L = 120, so L = 10 m.

options.A: That is the side of the tripled square.
options.C: That is 120 / 3.
options.D: Would be right if the tripled side were 60 (perimeter 240).

text: In a class, there are 80 students who have taken science which is 40% of the total strength. 20% of students have taken maths and the remaining students have taken english. How many students have taken english?

explain.why: 80 students are 40% of the class, so the class has 200 students. Maths is 20%, which is 40 students. English is the other 40%: 200 − 80 − 40 = 80.

options.B: That is 80 × 5, not the number of students who took English.
options.C: That is the total strength of the class.
options.D: That is the number taking maths.

text: Find the next number of the sequence 1, 5, 13, 25, _______

explain.why: The differences are 4, 8, 12, so the next difference is 16. The next number is 25 + 16 = 41.

options.A: Would be right if the next difference were 4, not 16.
options.C: Would be right if the next difference were 8, not 16.
options.D: Would be right if the next difference were 12, not 16.

text: If the perimeter of the square is 100, what is the area of the square?

explain.why: A square with perimeter 100 has side 100 / 4 = 25. Its area is 25 × 25 = 625.

options.A: That is 100².
options.B: That is 50², from half of the perimeter.
options.D: That is 100 × 10, not 25 × 25.

text: If the circumference of the circle is 31.4, what is the area of the circle?

explain.why: The circumference 2πr = 31.4 gives r = 5. The area is πr² = 3.14 × 25 = 78.5.

options.B: That is 31.4 × 10.
options.C: That is about 5π, the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 5.
options.D: That is about 5π, the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 5.

text: What is the golden value ratio?

explain.why: The golden ratio is about 1.618.

options.B: The digits of 1.618 in a different order.
options.C: The digits of 1.618 in a different order.

text: Choose the odd one out. 1, 2, 3, 5

explain.why: 2, 3 and 5 are prime numbers. 1 is not prime, so 1 is the odd one out.

options.B: 5 is prime.
options.C: 3 is prime.

text: If the radius has doubled the area of the circle will?

explain.why: The area is πr². If the radius doubles to 2r, the area is π(2r)² = 4πr², which is 4 times as much.

options.A: That would be true for the circumference.
options.C: Would be right if the area grew like r³, but it grows like r².
options.D: Would be right if the area grew like r⁴, but it grows like r².

text: If 8 – 8 =63 and 6 – 6 =35 then find the value of 11 – 11=?

explain.why: Each result is one less than the square of the number: 8² − 1 = 63 and 6² − 1 = 35. So 11² − 1 = 120.

options.A: Does not follow n² − 1, which gives 120.
options.C: Does not follow n² − 1, which gives 120.
options.D: Does not follow n² − 1, which gives 120.

text: PARLE is related to QCUPJ in the same way as DABUR is related to \_\_\_\_\_\_.

explain.why: In PARLE → QCUPJ each letter moves forward by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 places (P→Q, A→C, R→U, L→P, E→J). Applying the same to DABUR gives D+1 = E, A+2 = C, B+3 = E, U+4 = Y, R+5 = W: ECEYW.

options.A: Not DABUR with its letters moved by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 places, which gives ECEYW.
options.B: Not DABUR with its letters moved by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 places, which gives ECEYW.
options.C: Not DABUR with its letters moved by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 places, which gives ECEYW.

text: A clock shows 5 o'clock in the evening. How many degrees would the hour hand have rotated when the clock shows 11 o'clock at night?

explain.why: From 5 pm to 11 pm is 6 hours. The hour hand turns 30° each hour, so it turns 6 × 30 = 180°.

options.A: That is 4 hours.
options.B: That is 5 hours.
options.D: That is 7 hours.

text: What will be the circumference of a circle inscribed inside a square of side 23m ?

explain.why: A circle inscribed in a square of side 23 m has a diameter of 23 m. Its circumference is π × 23 = 23π.

options.A: That is the circumference for a diameter of 10, not 23.
options.B: That is the radius times π, 11.5π, not the circumference.
options.D: That is for a diameter of 46.

text: In a company, 50% of the employees like coffee, 20% like tea, and 10% like both. If 80 employees are working in the company, how many employees like neither coffee nor tea?

explain.why: Of 80 employees, 40 like coffee, 16 like tea and 8 like both. Those who like at least one are 40 + 16 − 8 = 48. So 80 − 48 = 32 like neither.

options.A: That is the number who like tea.
options.C: That would be 25% of 80; the share that likes neither is 40%.
options.D: That would be 30% of 80; the share that likes neither is 40%.

text: How many squares are there in the following image?

explain.why: Counting in the picture: 1 outer square, 14 in the inner 3 × 3 block (9 small, 4 of 2 × 2, 1 of 3 × 3), 4 corner squares, 4 larger corner squares and 4 squares at the middle of each side. That makes 1 + 14 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 27.

options.A: The picture has 27 squares, not 25.
options.C: The picture has 27 squares, not 28.
options.D: The picture has 27 squares, not 26.

text: Two notebooks of same price were bought for Rs. 74.8 at a discount of 15%. What is the original price of each of the notebooks ?

explain.why: At a 15% discount the buyer pays 85% of the original price. The total paid is 74.8, so the original total is 74.8 / 0.85 = 88. For two notebooks, each costs 88 / 2 = 44.

options.A: That is 88 / 4.
options.C: Two notebooks cost 88 at the original price, so each costs 44, not 66.
options.D: Two notebooks cost 88 at the original price, so each costs 44, not 11.

text: A metro train 55 meters long is running at a speed of 120 kmph. In what time will it pass a woman who is jogging at 3 kmph in the direction opposite to that in which the train is going?

explain.why: The train and the woman move in opposite directions, so the speeds add: 120 + 3 = 123 km/h = 123 × 5/18 ≈ 34.2 m/s. The train must cover its own length of 55 m, which takes 55 / 34.2 ≈ 1.6 seconds.

options.A: 55 m at 123 km/h takes about 1.6 s, not 2.4 s.
options.B: 55 m at 123 km/h takes about 1.6 s, not 3.2 s.
options.D: 55 m at 123 km/h takes about 1.6 s, not 1.2 s.

text:
Choose the correct option to fill in the blank.
The radius of a wheel is 3m. The wheel rolls 14 times in a minute. To cover a distance of 5.280 km, the wheel will take \_\_\_\_ minutes.

explain.why: The circumference of the wheel is 2π × 3 = 6π ≈ 18.86 m, so 14 rolls cover about 264 m in a minute. The distance 5.280 km is 5280 m, and 5280 / 264 = 20 minutes.

options.A: 5280 m at about 264 m per minute takes 20 minutes, not 10.
options.C: 5280 m at about 264 m per minute takes 20 minutes, not 5.
options.D: 5280 m at about 264 m per minute takes 20 minutes, not 25.

text: Ramesh decides to add tiles to a rectangle-shaped floor that measures 90m x 74m. To add the tiles, the mason charges Rs.11 per sq.m. Find the amount that Ramesh needs to pay the mason.

explain.why: The floor area is 90 × 74 = 6660 square metres. At Rs. 11 per square metre the cost is 6660 × 11 = Rs. 73260.

text: If the radius of a circle doubles, how does the area of the circle change?

explain.why: The area is πr². With the radius doubled, the area is π(2r)² = 4πr², which is 4 times as large.

options.A: That would be true for the circumference, which grows with r.
options.C: Would be right if the area grew like r³, but it grows like r².
options.D: Would be right if the area grew like r⁴, but it grows like r².
